To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of respondents are satisfied with their job and they have no intention to leave their jobs.
there is no gender difference in job satisfaction and there is a qualification difference in job satisfaction in secondary schools in Mbule.
there is no significant difference between graduate and nongraduate teachers regarding their job satifaction in secondary schools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between job satisfaction and teachers' job performance.
the factors that contribute to job satisfaction of teachers.
the factors that influence the job satisfaction of teachers, in selected secondary schools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the teachers in selected secondary school in Mbale town are generally satisfied with their jobs and that the factors that contribute to this are the intrinsic factors (professional advancement and professional development) and the extrinsic factors (interpersonal relationship, working conditions, supervison and remuneration).
, there is no difference in job satisfaction between male and female and graduate and non graduate secondary school teachers in selected secondary school in Mbale town.
, the factors influencing job satistaction of teachers in selected secodary schools, in Mbule town, are remuneration, working condition, professional development and interpersonal relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

job satisfaction of teachers is influenced by the following factors; remuneration, working condition, supervision, interpersonal relationship and professional development, it is recommended that, there is need to increase salaries of teachers and to ensure that teachers are given opportunities for professional development.

, job satisfaction among teachers in the selected secondary schools in M bale town is influenced by both intrinsic and extrinsic factors, the study recommends that the ministry of education and sports should provide teachers with adequate remuneration, working environment, professional development and supervision.

, the teachers in the selected schools are not fully satisfied, the teachers in these schools are satisfied with the instructional performance and the interpersonal relationship with their colleagues, the teachers are not satisfied with the relationship with their administrators, they are not satisfied with non teaching tasks, they are not fully satisfied with the working conditions, they are not satisfled with remuneration and they are not satisfied, with professional development.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a significant difference between the graduate and non-graduate teachers regarding job satisfaction in selected schools in Mbale, the study also revealed that the teachers in selected schools are not satisfied with their jobs.
the factors influencing job satistfaction are not gender specific, but are more related to academic qualifications.
the job satisfaction is a very important factor for teacher's performance.
